input.title: The Powerhouse stack offers a local-first event-sourced engine with browser and server hosts, generated APIs, and pluggable read models

input.description: Feature-surface overview of the Powerhouse stack at v6.2.2-dev.45: Reactor engine, Connect/Switchboard/Vetra hosts, codegen, processors, analytics, identity, attachments, and MCP.

input.content:
## One engine, two faces, one package

The Powerhouse stack is a **local-first, event-sourced application platform**. Everything below is built on one idea: state is never written directly — it is derived by replaying an immutable log of typed operations.

## Core engine

- **Reactor** — runs reducers, appends operations to storage, drives processors, and syncs with peer Reactors over the DocSync protocol. Storage-agnostic and modular; loads document models at runtime.
- **Operation sync, not state sync** — offline edits replay on the remote Reactor, so both ends converge without last-write-wins or manual merges.
- **Pluggable operation stores** — including a Hypercore-backed store (`reactor-hypercore`) alongside the default.

## Host applications

- **Connect** — browser collaboration workspace embedding a Reactor, so it works offline and syncs on reconnect. Renders your editors and drive-apps.
- **Switchboard** — server host exposing the Reactor over **GraphQL** and **MCP**. Runs processors and maintains read models.
- **Vetra** — the agent-first builder platform and local dev environment (Vetra Studio + Vetra Switchboard), spec-driven and AI-native.
- **Fusion** and **Renown** round out the four host applications.

## What builders ship

A single **package** bundles document models (schemas + reducers), editors, processors, and subgraphs, and plugs into all three layers at once: the Reactor runs the reducers, Connect renders the editors, Switchboard runs the processors.

## Feature surface by area

| Area | What the stack offers |
|---|---|
| Modelling | GraphQL-defined document models with typed operations, scoped state (global/local), and versioning/migration support |
| Codegen | `codegen` generates TypeScript types, reducers, and editor scaffolding from the GraphQL spec |
| API | `reactor-api` auto-generates a GraphQL subgraph per document model, plus the core reactor subgraph |
| Read models | Processors fold the operation stream into queryable projections; relational processors are backed by PGlite |
| Analytics | `analytics-engine` for time-series/dimensional analysis over document data |
| Client | `reactor-browser` provides React hooks and `IReactorClient` for editors and drive-apps |
| Identity | `renown` — wallet-based authentication and identity; document permissions, signing, and subgraph-level authorization |
| Attachments | `reactor-attachments` — content-addressed storage that keeps large binaries out of the action pipeline |
| Groups | `reactor-group` — group membership referenced by `{ group }` principals in the auth scope |
| AI integration | `reactor-mcp` exposes document model operations and drive management to AI coding agents over MCP |
| Design system | `design-system` / document-engineering — GraphQL scalar UI components |
| Tooling | `ph-cli` / `ph-cmd`, `builder-tools` (Vite + TS config, dev server), `registry` for package dependency resolution |

## Version context

Describes the stack at **v6.2.2-dev.45** (2026-08-13). Most other Powerhouse knowledge in this vault is baselined at v6.0.0-dev.254 — see the corpus baseline note.
